tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

<system-reminder>

Otherwise carry on with the request and do not mention these servers. Do not ask the user for authorization codes, tokens, or callback URLs.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

235	the unchanged state. -/
236	inductive Run (k : K) : S3 → List KernelOp → List (Outcome3 Unit) → S3 → Prop
237	  | nil {s : S3} : Run k s [] [] s
238	  | ok {s t u : S3} {op : KernelOp} {ops : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} :
239	      op.Step k s (.ok t) → Run k t ops vs u → Run k s (op :: ops) (.ok () :: vs) u

273	
274	Dependency kinds:
275	**idx** reads identities by equality or membership only (needs `SRel`);
276	**range** quantifies over `List.range |P|` or `List.range |A|` (needs the bijection of the range,
277	`PRel.lt_iff`, `SRel.Alt`);
278	**chain** follows links with an index check and fuel bounded by the index (needs `Down s`,
279	`Down s'`);
280	**pos** reads positions in an index-ordered list (needs `SibMono`);
281	**set** list result whose order depends on the numbering (stated with `Perm` or membership);
282	**fresh** creates identities `|P|`, `|A|`, `nF`, `|pins|` (needs `PRel.fix`, `SRel.Afix`);
283	**ind** inductive predicate (forward by induction, then symmetry);
284	**fuel** fuel `|P| + 1` (`pframeF`), read through `pframe_iff`;
285	**frames** frame identities, not renamed;
286	**K** reads `K`.

# Rename foundation (T0a, T0b, T0c): exported API

Files (all build, no `sorry`; `lake build Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.Derived` succeeds):

- `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Rename/Basic.lean`   (`import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main`)
- `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Rename/Places.lean`  (`import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.Basic`)
- `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Rename/Derived.lean` (`import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.Places`)

Not yet imported from `formal/Ern.lean` (T7 does that).

## Namespaces

Everything is in `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename`, except the four functions
`Holder.ren`, `Place.ren`, `K.rename`, `KernelOp.ren` (in `Ern.MemoryModel.Access`, so dot
notation works: `o.ren π`, `pl.ren π`, `k.rename π α`, `op.ren π α`).
Lemmas *about* them are in `Rename` too: `Rename.Holder.ren_symm`, `Rename.KernelOp.ren_symm_ren`, …
(call them as `Holder.ren_symm π o` from inside `namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename`; dot
notation `o.ren_symm` does NOT work).

Recommended header for wave-1 files:

```lean
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.Derived
namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename
variable {π α : Ren} {s s' : S3} {k k' : K}
```

**Name-shadowing pitfall (observed).** Inside the signature/body of a declaration named
`SRel.foo` (resp. `PRel.foo`), a short name `bar` resolves to `SRel.bar` (resp. `PRel.bar`) when
it exists. Kernel names shadowed this way: `effective`, `depsOf`, `mem_descModes`,
`mem_footprint`, `parentOf`. Write `Access.effective`, `Access.depsOf`, `Access.mem_descModes`,
`Access.mem_footprint`, `Access.parentOf` there. Dot notation on states (`s.pin`, `s.org`, `s.ancs`,
`s.pframe`, …) is not affected.

## Conventions

`h : SRel π α s s'`, `hd : Down s`, `hd' : Down s'`, `hS : Sim π α s s'` (`hS.rel`, `hS.down`,
`hS.down'`, `hS.sib`), `hK : KCorr π α k k'`; place-level: `hP : PRel π P P'`, `hd : DownP P`,
`hd' : DownP P'`, `hs : SibMono π P`. From a `Sim`: `hS.rel.P`, `hS.down.1`, `hS.down'.1`.
"f-form" `π.f l ∈ L' ↔ l ∈ L`; g-form via `Ren.mem_iff_g`.
Closing an iff by symmetry: `h.symm : SRel π.symm α.symm s' s`; `Ren.symm_f : π.symm.f i = π.g i`
(simp) and `π.gf`: e.g. `fun h' => by simpa only [Ren.symm_f, π.gf] using h.symm.usable_of h'`.
For closed statements (no renamed argument), `h.symm.foo_of hd' hd` directly.

## Basic.lean — definitions (as in design §3)

```lean
structure Ren where
  f : Nat → Nat
  g : Nat → Nat
  gf : ∀ i, g (f i) = i
  fg : ∀ i, f (g i) = i
def Ren.id : Ren
def Ren.symm (π : Ren) : Ren                          -- ⟨π.g, π.f, π.fg, π.gf⟩
def Ren.comp (π' π : Ren) : Ren                       -- f i = π'.f (π.f i)
def Ren.ofPerm (τ : List Nat) (n : Nat) (h : τ.Perm (List.range n)) : Ren
  -- f x = if x < n then τ.idxOf x else x;  g i = if i < τ.length then τ[i] else i

def Holder.ren (π : Ren) : Holder → Holder            -- frames kept, .place p ↦ .place (π.f p)
def Place.ren (π : Ren) (pl : Place) : Place := ⟨pl.parent.map π.f, pl.owner.ren π, pl.kind⟩

structure AuthRel (π α : Ren) (y y' : Authority) : Prop where
  mode : y'.mode = y.mode
  origin : y'.origin = y.origin.map α.f
  footprint : y'.footprint.Perm (y.footprint.map π.f)
  holder : y'.holder = y.holder.ren π
  active : y'.active = y.active
structure PinRel (π : Ren) (ob ob' : PinOb) : Prop where
  place : ob'.place = π.f ob.place
  leaves : ob'.leaves.Perm (ob.leaves.map π.f)
  active : ob'.active = ob.active
structure PRel (π : Ren) (P P' : List Place) : Prop where
  len : P'.length = P.length
  get : ∀ q, P'[π.f q]? = (P[q]?).map (Place.ren π)
  fix : ∀ q, P.length ≤ q → π.f q = q
structure SRel (π α : Ren) (s s' : S3) : Prop where
  F : s'.F = s.F
  nF : s'.nF = s.nF
  P : PRel π s.P s'.P
  I : ∀ l, s'.I (π.f l) = s.I l
  Alen : s'.A.length = s.A.length
  A : ∀ x, Option.Rel (AuthRel π α) (s.A[x]?) (s'.A[α.f x]?)
  Afix : ∀ x, s.A.length ≤ x → α.f x = x
  D : ∀ q, (s'.D (π.f q)).Perm ((s.D q).map α.f)
  dead : ∀ q, s'.dead (π.f q) = s.dead q
  pins : ∀ o : Nat, Option.Rel (PinRel π) (s.pins[o]?) (s'.pins[o]?)
def DownP (P : List Place) : Prop := ∀ j o, parentOf P j = some o → o < j
def DownA (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ j o, s.org j = some o → o < j
def Down (s : S3) : Prop := DownP s.P ∧ DownA s
def SibMono (π : Ren) (P : List Place) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y p, parentOf P x = some p → parentOf P y = some p → x < y → π.f x < π.f y
structure Sim (π α : Ren) (s s' : S3) : Prop where
  rel : SRel π α s s'
  down : Down s
  down' : Down s'
  sib : SibMono π s.P
def KExt (k : K) : Prop :=
  ∀ p sh s t, SRel Ren.id Ren.id s t → k.Satisfiable p sh s → k.Satisfiable p sh t
def K.rename (π α : Ren) (k : K) : K where
  DeclaredDisjoint r r' := k.DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.g) (r'.map π.g)
  SharedMutable l := k.SharedMutable (π.g l)
  Pinned l := k.Pinned (π.g l)
  ExternalDone o := k.ExternalDone o
  Deallocable p := k.Deallocable (π.g p)
  FreeCompat p a := k.FreeCompat (π.g p) a
  Satisfiable p sh t := ∃ t₀, SRel π α t₀ t ∧ k.Satisfiable (π.g p) sh t₀
def KernelOp.ren (π α : Ren) : KernelOp → KernelOp    -- exactly the table of design §3
structure KCorr (π α : Ren) (k k' : K) : Prop where
  dd : ∀ r r', k'.DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.f) (r'.map π.f) ↔ k.DeclaredDisjoint r r'
  shared : ∀ l, k'.SharedMutable (π.f l) ↔ k.SharedMutable l
  pinned : ∀ l, k'.Pinned (π.f l) ↔ k.Pinned l
  done : ∀ o, k'.ExternalDone o ↔ k.ExternalDone o
  dealloc : ∀ p, k'.Deallocable (π.f p) ↔ k.Deallocable p
  compat : ∀ p a, k'.FreeCompat (π.f p) a ↔ k.FreeCompat p a
def OutRel (π α : Ren) : Outcome3 S3 → Outcome3 S3 → Prop   -- ok/ok: SRel; reject/reject, fail/fail: True
def StepCorr (π α : Ren) (R R' : Outcome3 S3 → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ o, R o → ∃ o', R' o' ∧ OutRel π α o o') ∧ ∀ o', R' o' → ∃ o, R o ∧ OutRel π α o o'
```

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.DeriveSplitRelease
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Transfer
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Small

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.EndFree

/-!
# Access kernel: steps, reachable states and the main invariant

Assembles the per-operation results of `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.*` into the statements of
§57, §58 and §59 of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`:

* kernel operations O1–O16 as data, their outcome relation, and the correspondence of `KStep` and
  `Reachable` with the labelled steps and their reflexive-transitive closure (§57, §58);
* preservation of `KInv` (§57) by every step, `transfer` (§63) included, from states satisfying
  `KInv` and the auxiliary `HeldAnchored`; preservation of the auxiliaries `KAux` and
  `HeldAnchored` by every step; preservation of `I5` (§57) by every step from a `WF3` state;
* the initial state satisfies the invariant and the auxiliaries under `StaticsOK` (§47), and its
  `Init` leaves are the declared ones;
* the main invariant on reachable states (§57, `reachable_kinv`) and `I5` on reachable states
  (`reachable_i5`); the ownership-cycle run of §63 is rejected by §63.9
  (`reachable_cycle_rejected`);
* §59: only writes and transfers make a leaf `Init`, and every `Init` leaf of a reached state was
  declared or written on the run; §39: frame 0 stays at the bottom of the stack; §58: only `alloc`
  fails.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Kernel operations as data (§58, §60–§75) -/

/-- A kernel operation O1–O16 with its arguments (§60–§75). -/
inductive KernelOp where
  /-- O1 `derive` (§60). -/
  | derive (src : Nat) (region : List Nat) (m : Mode)
  /-- O2 `split` (§61). -/
  | split (src : Nat) (rs : List (List Nat))
  /-- O3 `release` (§62). -/
  | release (a : Nat)
  /-- O4 `transfer` (§63). -/
  | transfer (src dst : Nat)
  /-- O5 `depend` (§64). -/
  | depend (q x : Nat)
  /-- O6 `enterFrame` (§72). -/
  | enter (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
  /-- O7 `exitFrame` (§73). -/
  | exit
  /-- O9 `read` (§66). -/
  | read (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  /-- O10 `write` (§67). -/
  | write (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  /-- O11 `writeShared` (§68). -/
  | writeShared (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  /-- O15 `pin` (§74). -/
  | pin (p : Nat)
  /-- O16 `unpin` (§75), designating the dynamic pinning obligation of identity `o`. -/
  | unpin (o : Nat)
  /-- O12 `endUse` (§69). -/
  | endUse (p : Nat)
  /-- O13 `free` (§70). -/
  | free (p auth : Nat)
  /-- O14 `alloc` (§71). -/
  | alloc (pr ow : Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
  /-- O8 `store` (§65). -/
  | store (a p : Nat)

/-- Outcome relation of a kernel operation (§58, §60–§75): the step relation of the operation. -/
def KernelOp.Step (k : K) : KernelOp → S3 → Outcome3 S3 → Prop
  | .derive src region m => DeriveStep src region m
  | .split src rs => SplitStep k src rs
  | .release a => ReleaseStep a
  | .transfer src dst => TransferStep k src dst
  | .depend q x => DependStep q x
  | .enter ps ls => EnterStep ps ls
  | .exit => ExitStep k
  | .read a ls => Read3Step a ls
  | .write a ls => Write3Step a ls
  | .writeShared a ls => WriteSharedStep k a ls
  | .pin p => PinStep p
  | .unpin o => UnpinStep k o
  | .endUse p => EndUseStep k p
  | .free p auth => FreeStep k p auth
  | .alloc pr ow ls => AllocStep k pr ow ls
  | .store a p => StoreStep a p

/-- A kernel step is the `ok` outcome of some operation O1–O16 (§57, §58). -/
theorem kstep_iff {k : K} {s s' : S3} : KStep k s s' ↔ ∃ op : KernelOp, op.Step k s (.ok s') := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    cases h with
    | derive h => exact ⟨.derive _ _ _, h⟩
    | split h => exact ⟨.split _ _, h⟩
    | release h => exact ⟨.release _, h⟩
    | transfer h => exact ⟨.transfer _ _, h⟩
    | depend h => exact ⟨.depend _ _, h⟩
    | enter h => exact ⟨.enter _ _, h⟩
    | exit h => exact ⟨.exit, h⟩
    | read h => exact ⟨.read _ _, h⟩
    | write h => exact ⟨.write _ _, h⟩
    | writeShared h => exact ⟨.writeShared _ _, h⟩
    | pin h => exact ⟨.pin _, h⟩
    | unpin h => exact ⟨.unpin _, h⟩
    | endUse h => exact ⟨.endUse _, h⟩
    | free h => exact ⟨.free _ _, h⟩
    | alloc h => exact ⟨.alloc _ _ _, h⟩
    | store h => exact ⟨.store _ _, h⟩
  · rintro ⟨op, h⟩
    cases op with
    | derive => exact .derive h
    | split => exact .split h
    | release => exact .release h
    | transfer => exact .transfer h
    | depend => exact .depend h
    | enter => exact .enter h
    | exit => exact .exit h
    | read => exact .read h
    | write => exact .write h
    | writeShared => exact .writeShared h
    | pin => exact .pin h
    | unpin => exact .unpin h
    | endUse => exact .endUse h
    | free => exact .free h
    | alloc => exact .alloc h
    | store => exact .store h

/-- Finite runs of kernel steps from `s` (§57): the reflexive-transitive closure of `KStep`. -/
inductive KStar (k : K) (s : S3) : S3 → Prop where
  /-- The empty run (§57). -/
  | refl : KStar k s s
  /-- A run followed by one kernel step (§57). -/
  | tail {t u : S3} : KStar k s t → KStep k t u → KStar k s u

/-- The reachable states of §57 are the states reached from `S3.init statics` by a finite run of
kernel steps. -/
theorem reachable_iff {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} :
    Reachable k statics s ↔ KStar k (S3.init statics) s := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    induction h with
    | init => exact .refl
    | step _ h ih => exact .tail ih h
  · intro h
    induction h with
    | refl => exact .init
    | tail _ h ih => exact .step ih h

/-! ## Outcomes (§58) and the base frame (§39) -/

/-- Only `alloc` may produce `fail` among O1–O16 (§58). -/
theorem op_fail_only_alloc {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s : S3} (h : op.Step k s .fail) :
    ∃ pr ow ls, op = .alloc pr ow ls := by
  cases op with
  | alloc pr ow ls => exact ⟨pr, ow, ls, rfl⟩
  | _ => exact (Alloc.guarded_ne_fail h).elim

/-- No kernel step changes the bottom of the frame stack (§39: the base frame never exits). -/
theorem kstep_base {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : KStep k s s') : s'.F.getLast? = s.F.getLast? := by
  cases h with
  | derive h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | split h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | release h =>
    rename_i a
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    unfold releaseEff; split <;> rfl
  | transfer h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | depend h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | enter h => exact enter_keeps_base h
  | exit h => exact (exit_keeps_base h).2
  | read h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | write h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | writeShared h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | pin h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | unpin h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | endUse h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | free h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rfl
  | alloc h => cases h with | ok => rfl
  | store h =>
    rename_i a p
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    unfold storeEff; split <;> rfl

/-- On every reachable state, the bottom of the stack is the base frame 0 (§39, §47). -/
theorem reachable_base {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (h : Reachable k statics s) :
    s.F.getLast? = some 0 := by
  induction h with
  | init => rfl
  | step _ h ih => rw [kstep_base h]; exact ih

/-- The base frame 0 is never removed from the stack of a reachable state (§39). -/
theorem reachable_base_mem {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (h : Reachable k statics s) :
    0 ∈ s.F :=
  List.mem_of_getLast? (reachable_base h)

/-! ## Preservation by every step (§57, §58) -/

/-- Every operation, `transfer` included, preserves `KInv` (§57) from a state satisfying `KInv`
and the auxiliary `HeldAnchored` (not a clause of §57, used by `transfer`, §63) to its `ok`
outcome, under `DDSound` (§80, used by `split`, §61). -/
theorem op_preserves {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k) (hinv : KInv s)

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Invariants

/-!
# Access kernel: conforming statics declarations and their numbering

`StaticsConf` is the conformance of a statics declaration to §47 and §49 with no order between
identifiers. `StaticsOK` (`Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Invariants`) asks parents and owning statics to
be earlier statics; by §49 (last paragraph) this ordering only represents well-formedness. Every
conforming declaration has a consistent renumbering satisfying `StaticsOK`
(`StaticsConf.exists_renumber`), and every declaration satisfying `StaticsOK` conforms
(`StaticsConf.of_staticsOK`).
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Conformance (§40, §47, §49) -/

/-- Structural parent of static `i` (§40): `none` for a root static or an index outside the
declaration. -/
def staticParent (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (statics[i]?).bind (·.1.1)

/-- Owning static of static `i` (§40, §47): `none` for a static owned by frame 0 or an index
outside the declaration. -/
def staticOwner (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (statics[i]?).bind (·.1.2.1)

/-- Conformance of a statics declaration to §47 and §49, with no order between identifiers
(§49, last paragraph). Owners are frame 0 or a static (§40, §47), parents and owning statics are
declared statics (§49.2, §49.3), composition links are acyclic (§49.2), no static is owned,
directly or transitively, by itself (§47), and every structural part has its parent's owner
(§49.2, §40).

Acyclicity is the irreflexivity of the transitive closure `Relation.TransGen` of the one-step
link (`a`'s parent, resp. owning static, is `b`): `TransGen link i i` holds exactly when a
nonempty chain of links leads from `i` back to `i`, which is what §47 ("owned, directly or
transitively, by itself") and §49.2 (acyclic composition links) exclude. No bound on chain
length is involved. -/
structure StaticsConf (statics : Statics) : Prop where
  /-- §49.2: composition links are valid; every structural parent is a declared static. -/
  parent_lt : ∀ i p, staticParent statics i = some p → p < statics.length
  /-- §49.3, §47: owners are valid; every owning static is a declared static. -/
  owner_lt : ∀ i o, staticOwner statics i = some o → o < statics.length
  /-- §49.2: composition links are acyclic; no static is its own strict structural ancestor. -/
  parent_acyclic : ∀ i, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => staticParent statics a = some b) i i
  /-- §47: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. -/
  owner_acyclic : ∀ i, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => staticOwner statics a = some b) i i
  /-- §49.2, §40: every structural part shares its parent's owner. -/
  part_owner : ∀ i p, staticParent statics i = some p →
    staticOwner statics i = staticOwner statics p

/-! ## Renumbering (§49, last paragraph; §63.2) -/

/-- A static's entry with its references, parent and owning static, mapped through `τ`; its
kind and initial state are kept (§49, last paragraph). -/
def mapRefs (τ : Nat → Nat) (e : (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool) :
    (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool :=
  ((e.1.1.map τ, e.1.2.1.map τ, e.1.2.2), e.2)

/-- Renumbering of a declaration by `σ` (§49, last paragraph): new index `i` holds old static
`σ[i]`, its parent and owning static mapped through the inverse `σ.idxOf`. Meant for `σ` a
permutation of `List.range statics.length`. -/
def renumber (σ : List Nat) (statics : Statics) : Statics :=
  σ.map fun j => mapRefs σ.idxOf ((statics[j]?).getD ((none, none, 0), false))

/-- Consistent renumbering (§49, last paragraph; §63.2): the new index `σ.idxOf x` of every old
static `x` holds `x` with its parent and owning static mapped through `σ.idxOf`, and its kind and
initial state; the parts of every place keep their relative order, which is their positional
field order (§63.2; `kids` orders the parts of a place by index). -/
structure ConsistentRenumbering (σ : List Nat) (statics : Statics) : Prop where
  /-- Parents to parents, owning statics to owning statics, same kind and initial state. -/
  entry : ∀ x < statics.length,
    (renumber σ statics)[σ.idxOf x]? = (statics[x]?).map (mapRefs σ.idxOf)
  /-- §63.2: the field order of every place is preserved. -/
  field_order : ∀ x y p, staticParent statics x = some p → staticParent statics y = some p →
    x < y → σ.idxOf x < σ.idxOf y

/-! ## Proof support: chains of a partial link -/

/-- Pigeonhole: a duplicate-free list of numbers below `n` has at most `n` elements. -/
private theorem nodup_length_le : ∀ (n : Nat) (l : List Nat), l.Nodup → (∀ a ∈ l, a < n) →
    l.length ≤ n
  | 0, [], _, _ => Nat.le_refl _
  | 0, a :: _, _, h => absurd (h a (List.mem_cons_self ..)) (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, l, hd, h => by
    have := nodup_length_le n (l.erase n) (hd.erase n) fun a ha => by
      rw [hd.mem_erase_iff] at ha
      have := h a ha.2
      omega
    rw [List.length_erase] at this
    split at this <;> omega

/-- `k` links `f` from `x`. -/
private def iter (f : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → Option Nat
  | 0, x => some x
  | k + 1, x => (iter f k x).bind f

private theorem iter_add (f : Nat → Option Nat) (x i : Nat) : ∀ d,
    iter f (i + d) x = (iter f i x).bind (iter f d)
  | 0 => by
    show iter f i x = _
    cases iter f i x <;> rfl
  | d + 1 => by
    show (iter f (i + d) x).bind f = _
    rw [iter_add f x i d, Option.bind_assoc]
    rfl

private theorem transGen_of_iter {f : Nat → Option Nat} {x : Nat} : ∀ {k y : Nat},
    iter f (k + 1) x = some y → Relation.TransGen (fun a b => f a = some b) x y
  | 0, _, h => .single h
  | k + 1, _, h => by
    obtain ⟨c, hc, hcy⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.1 h
    exact .tail (transGen_of_iter hc) hcy

/-- An acyclic partial link whose targets are below `n` has chains of fewer than `n` links from
any `x < n`. -/
private theorem iter_bound {f : Nat → Option Nat} {n : Nat}
    (hacyc : ∀ a, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => f a = some b) a a)
    (hlt : ∀ a b, f a = some b → b < n) {x : Nat} (hx : x < n) {k : Nat}
    (hk : (iter f k x).isSome) : k < n := by
  let g := fun i => (iter f i x).getD 0
  have hsome : ∀ i ≤ k, iter f i x = some (g i) := by
    intro i hi
    have := iter_add f x i (k - i)
    rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel' hi] at this
    cases hc : iter f i x with
    | none => rw [hc] at this; rw [this] at hk; simp at hk
    | some c => simp [g, hc]
  have hlt' : ∀ a ∈ (List.range (k + 1)).map g, a < n := by
    intro a ha
    obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 ha
    have hi' := hsome i (by rw [List.mem_range] at hi; omega)
    cases i with
    | zero => simp only [iter, Option.some.injEq] at hi'; omega
    | succ j =>
      obtain ⟨c, -, hc⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.1 hi'
      exact hlt c _ hc
  have hnd : ((List.range (k + 1)).map g).Nodup := by
    unfold List.Nodup
    rw [List.pairwise_map]
    refine List.pairwise_lt_range.imp_of_mem fun {i j} hi hj hij heq => ?_
    rw [List.mem_range] at hi hj
    have hj' := iter_add f x i (j - i)
    rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel' (Nat.le_of_lt hij), hsome i (by omega), hsome j (by omega), heq,
      Option.bind_some] at hj'
    obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ : ∃ d, j - i = d + 1 := ⟨j - i - 1, by omega⟩
    rw [hd] at hj'
    exact hacyc _ (transGen_of_iter hj'.symm)
  have := nodup_length_le n _ hnd hlt'
  simp only [List.length_map, List.length_range] at this
  omega

/-- Length of the chain of links `f` from `x`, cut at `k` links. -/
private def chainLen (f : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → Nat
  | 0, _ => 0
  | k + 1, x => match f x with
    | none => 0
    | some y => chainLen f k y + 1

private theorem chainLen_some {f : Nat → Option Nat} {k x y : Nat} (h : f x = some y) :
    chainLen f (k + 1) x = chainLen f k y + 1 := by
  show (match f x with | none => 0 | some y => chainLen f k y + 1) = _
  rw [h]

private theorem chainLen_congr {f : Nat → Option Nat} {x y : Nat} (h : f x = f y) :
    ∀ k, chainLen f k x = chainLen f k y
  | 0 => rfl
  | _ + 1 => by simp only [chainLen, h]

private theorem iter_of_chainLen_ne {f : Nat → Option Nat} : ∀ {k z : Nat},
    chainLen f (k + 1) z ≠ chainLen f k z → (iter f (k + 1) z).isSome
  | 0, z, h => by
    cases hz : f z with
    | none => simp [chainLen, hz] at h
    | some y => simp [iter, hz]
  | k + 1, z, h => by
    cases hz : f z with
    | none => simp [chainLen, hz] at h
    | some y =>
      rw [chainLen_some hz, chainLen_some hz] at h
      have := iter_add f z 1 (k + 1)
      rw [Nat.add_comm 1] at this
      rw [this]
      simp only [iter, Option.bind_some, hz]
      exact iter_of_chainLen_ne (by omega)

/-- Under an acyclic link with targets below `n`, the chain length cut at `n` grows by one along
each link. -/
private theorem chainLen_step {f : Nat → Option Nat} {n : Nat}
    (hacyc : ∀ a, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => f a = some b) a a)
    (hlt : ∀ a b, f a = some b → b < n) {x y : Nat} (h : f x = some y) :
    chainLen f n x = chainLen f n y + 1 := by
  have hy := hlt x y h
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 1 := ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
  rw [chainLen_some h]
  refine congrArg (· + 1) (Classical.byContradiction fun hne => ?_)
  have := iter_bound hacyc hlt hy (iter_of_chainLen_ne (k := m) (fun e => hne e.symm))
  omega

/-! ## Proof support: the order of a conforming declaration -/

/-- Ownership depth of a static. -/
private def odepth (statics : Statics) (x : Nat) : Nat :=
  chainLen (staticOwner statics) statics.length x

/-- Structural depth of a static. -/
private def sdepth (statics : Statics) (x : Nat) : Nat :=
  chainLen (staticParent statics) statics.length x

/-- Lexicographic order on (ownership depth, structural depth, index). -/
private def keyLe (statics : Statics) (a b : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (odepth statics a < odepth statics b ∨ odepth statics a = odepth statics b ∧
    (sdepth statics a < sdepth statics b ∨ sdepth statics a = sdepth statics b ∧ a ≤ b))

private theorem idxOf_lt_of_key {statics : Statics} {σ : List Nat}
    (hσ : σ.Perm (List.range statics.length)) (hs : σ.Pairwise (fun a b => keyLe statics a b))
    {x y : Nat} (hx : x < statics.length) (hy : y < statics.length)
    (hk : odepth statics x < odepth statics y ∨ odepth statics x = odepth statics y ∧
      (sdepth statics x < sdepth statics y ∨ sdepth statics x = sdepth statics y ∧ x < y)) :
    σ.idxOf x < σ.idxOf y := by
  have hix := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hσ.mem_iff.2 (List.mem_range.2 hx))
  have hiy := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hσ.mem_iff.2 (List.mem_range.2 hy))
  have gx := List.getElem_idxOf hix
  have gy := List.getElem_idxOf hiy
  rcases Nat.lt_trichotomy (σ.idxOf x) (σ.idxOf y) with h | h | h
  · exact h
  · have : x = y := by
      rw [← gx, ← gy]
      exact getElem_congr rfl h hix
    subst this
    omega
  · have := List.pairwise_iff_getElem.1 hs _ _ hiy hix h
    rw [gx, gy] at this
    simp only [keyLe, decide_eq_true_eq] at this
    omega

private theorem lt_of_parent {statics : Statics} {x p : Nat}
    (h : staticParent statics x = some p) : x < statics.length := by
  unfold staticParent at h
  cases hx : statics[x]? with
  | none => rw [hx] at h; cases h
  | some _ => exact (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 hx).1

private theorem lt_of_owner {statics : Statics} {x o : Nat}
    (h : staticOwner statics x = some o) : x < statics.length := by
  unfold staticOwner at h
  cases hx : statics[x]? with
  | none => rw [hx] at h; cases h
  | some _ => exact (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 hx).1

private theorem shape_parent (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) :
    ((statics.map (·.1))[i]?).bind (·.1) = staticParent statics i := by
  simp only [List.getElem?_map, staticParent]
  cases statics[i]? <;> rfl

private theorem shape_owner (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) :
    ((statics.map (·.1))[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = staticOwner statics i := by
  simp only [List.getElem?_map, staticOwner]
  cases statics[i]? <;> rfl

private theorem renumber_get {σ : List Nat} {statics : Statics} {i : Nat} (hi : i < σ.length)
    (hx : σ[i] < statics.length) :
    (renumber σ statics)[i]? = some (mapRefs σ.idxOf statics[σ[i]]) := by
  simp [renumber, hi, hx]

private theorem renumber_parent {σ : List Nat} {statics : Statics} {i : Nat} (hi : i < σ.length)
    (hx : σ[i] < statics.length) :
    staticParent (renumber σ statics) i = (staticParent statics σ[i]).map σ.idxOf := by
  rw [staticParent, renumber_get hi hx, staticParent, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hx]
  rfl

private theorem renumber_owner {σ : List Nat} {statics : Statics} {i : Nat} (hi : i < σ.length)
    (hx : σ[i] < statics.length) :
    staticOwner (renumber σ statics) i = (staticOwner statics σ[i]).map σ.idxOf := by
  rw [staticOwner, renumber_get hi hx, staticOwner, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hx]
  rfl

/-! ## Existence of a conforming numbering -/

/-- Owner decision of 2026-11-06 on `StaticsOK`, point (a) (§47, §49 and its last paragraph,
§63.2): every declaration conforming to §47 and §49 has a consistent renumbering, a permutation
of its identifiers preserving parents, owning statics, kinds, initial states and field order,
that satisfies `StaticsOK`. -/
theorem StaticsConf.exists_renumber {statics : Statics} (h : StaticsConf statics) :
    ∃ σ : List Nat, σ.Perm (List.range statics.length) ∧ ConsistentRenumbering σ statics ∧
      StaticsOK (renumber σ statics) := by
  let σ := (List.range statics.length).mergeSort (keyLe statics)
  have hσ : σ.Perm (List.range statics.length) := List.mergeSort_perm _ _
  have hs : σ.Pairwise (fun a b => keyLe statics a b) :=
    List.pairwise_mergeSort
      (fun a b c hab hbc => by simp only [keyLe, decide_eq_true_eq] at *; omega)
      (fun a b => by simp only [keyLe, Bool.or_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq]; omega) _
  have hnd : σ.Nodup := hσ.nodup_iff.2 List.nodup_range
  have hown : ∀ x o, staticOwner statics x = some o → odepth statics x = odepth statics o + 1 :=
    fun _ _ hxo => chainLen_step h.owner_acyclic h.owner_lt hxo
  have hpar : ∀ x p, staticParent statics x = some p → sdepth statics x = sdepth statics p + 1 :=
    fun _ _ hxp => chainLen_step h.parent_acyclic h.parent_lt hxp
  have hpo : ∀ x p, staticParent statics x = some p → odepth statics x = odepth statics p :=
    fun x p hxp => chainLen_congr (h.part_owner x p hxp) _
  refine ⟨σ, hσ, ⟨fun x hx => ?_, fun x y p hx hy hxy => ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · have hix := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hσ.mem_iff.2 (List.mem_range.2 hx))
    simp [renumber, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hix, List.getElem_idxOf hix,
      List.getElem?_eq_getElem hx]
  · have := hpar x p hx
    have := hpar y p hy
    have := hpo x p hx
    have := hpo y p hy
    exact idxOf_lt_of_key hσ hs (lt_of_parent hx) (lt_of_parent hy) (by omega)
  · unfold StaticsOK ShapeOK
    intro i hi
    simp only [List.length_map, renumber, List.mem_range] at hi
    have hxi : σ[i] < statics.length := List.mem_range.1 (hσ.mem_iff.1 (List.getElem_mem hi))
    have hii : σ.idxOf σ[i] = i :=
      (List.Nodup.getElem_inj hnd).1 (List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem
        (List.getElem_mem hi)))
    simp only [shape_parent, shape_owner, Nat.sub_zero, Nat.zero_add, renumber_parent hi hxi,
      renumber_owner hi hxi]
    constructor
    · cases hp : staticParent statics σ[i] with
      | none => trivial
      | some p =>
        have hpl := h.parent_lt _ _ hp
        have hip := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hσ.mem_iff.2 (List.mem_range.2 hpl))
        have hpσ : σ[σ.idxOf p] = p := List.getElem_idxOf hip
        refine ⟨Nat.zero_le _, ?_, ?_⟩
        · have := hpar _ _ hp
          have := hpo _ _ hp
          have := idxOf_lt_of_key hσ hs hpl hxi (by omega)
          show σ.idxOf p < i
          omega
        · show (staticOwner statics σ[i]).map σ.idxOf = staticOwner (renumber σ statics) (σ.idxOf p)
          rw [renumber_owner hip (by rw [hpσ]; exact hpl), hpσ, h.part_owner _ _ hp]
    · cases ho : staticOwner statics σ[i] with
      | none => trivial
      | some o =>
        have hol := h.owner_lt _ _ ho
        have := hown _ _ ho
        have := idxOf_lt_of_key hσ hs hol hxi (by omega)
        exact ⟨Nat.zero_le _, show σ.idxOf o < i by omega⟩

/-! ## `StaticsOK` declarations conform -/

private theorem rank_of_transGen {R : Nat → Nat → Prop} (rank : Nat → Nat)
    (h : ∀ a b, R a b → rank b < rank a) {a b : Nat} (hab : Relation.TransGen R a b) :
    rank b < rank a := by
  induction hab with
  | single hr => exact h _ _ hr
  | tail _ hr ih => exact Nat.lt_trans (h _ _ hr) ih

/-- `StaticsOK` (§47, §49) is a numbering of a conforming declaration: it implies
`StaticsConf`. -/
theorem StaticsConf.of_staticsOK {statics : Statics} (h : StaticsOK statics) :
    StaticsConf statics := by
  have hok : ∀ i, i < statics.length →
      OptP (staticParent statics i)
        (fun r => r < i ∧ staticOwner statics i = staticOwner statics r) True ∧
      OptP (staticOwner statics i) (fun o => o < i) True := by
    intro i hi
    have := h i (List.mem_range.2 (by simpa using hi))
    simp only [shape_parent, shape_owner, Nat.sub_zero, Nat.zero_add] at this
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := this
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · cases hp : staticParent statics i with
      | none => trivial
      | some r =>
        rw [hp] at h1
        obtain ⟨-, h3, h4⟩ := h1
        exact ⟨h3, h4⟩
    · cases ho : staticOwner statics i with
      | none => trivial
      | some o =>
        rw [ho] at h2
        exact h2.2
  have hpar : ∀ a b, staticParent statics a = some b → b < a := fun a b hab => by
    have := (hok a (lt_of_parent hab)).1
    rw [hab] at this
    exact this.1
  have hown : ∀ a b, staticOwner statics a = some b → b < a := fun a b hab => by
    have := (hok a (lt_of_owner hab)).2
    rw [hab] at this
    exact this
  exact {
    parent_lt := fun i p hp => Nat.lt_trans (hpar i p hp) (lt_of_parent hp)
    owner_lt := fun i o ho => Nat.lt_trans (hown i o ho) (lt_of_owner ho)
    parent_acyclic := fun _ hc => Nat.lt_irrefl _ (rank_of_transGen id hpar hc)
    owner_acyclic := fun _ hc => Nat.lt_irrefl _ (rank_of_transGen id hown hc)
    part_owner := fun i p hp => by
      have := (hok i (lt_of_parent hp)).1
      rw [hp] at this
      exact this.2 }

/-! ## Non-vacuity examples (§47, §49, §63.2) -/

namespace StaticsExamples

/-- Static 0 is a part of static 1, declared before it (§49, last paragraph). -/
def partFirst : Statics := [((some 1, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 1), false)]

/-- `partFirst` is not numbered parent first. -/
example : ¬ StaticsOK partFirst := by decide

private theorem partFirst_owner : ∀ i, staticOwner partFirst i = none
  | 0 | 1 | _ + 2 => rfl

/-- `partFirst` conforms to §47 and §49. -/
example : StaticsConf partFirst where
  parent_lt i p hp := by
    rcases i with _ | _ | i <;> simp [staticParent, partFirst] at hp ⊢
    omega
  owner_lt i o ho := by rw [partFirst_owner] at ho; cases ho
  parent_acyclic _ hc := Nat.lt_irrefl _ (rank_of_transGen (fun a => if a = 1 then 0 else 1)
    (fun a b hab => by
      rcases a with _ | _ | a <;> simp [staticParent, partFirst] at hab
      subst hab; decide) hc)
  owner_acyclic _ hc := Nat.lt_irrefl _ (rank_of_transGen (fun _ => 0)
    (fun a b hab => by rw [partFirst_owner] at hab; cases hab) hc)
  part_owner i p _ := by rw [partFirst_owner, partFirst_owner]

/-- Its renumbering by `[1, 0]` satisfies `StaticsOK`. -/
example : StaticsOK (renumber [1, 0] partFirst) := by decide

/-- Two fields 0 and 1 of static 2, declared before it (§63.2). -/
def fieldsFirst : Statics :=
  [((some 2, none, 0), true), ((some 2, none, 1), false), ((none, none, 2), false)]

/-- Swapping the fields gives a declaration satisfying `StaticsOK`, but not a consistent
renumbering: the field order clause is not vacuous (§63.2). -/
example : StaticsOK (renumber [2, 1, 0] fieldsFirst) ∧
    ¬ ConsistentRenumbering [2, 1, 0] fieldsFirst :=
  ⟨by decide, fun h => absurd (h.field_order 0 1 2 rfl rfl (by decide)) (by decide)⟩

/-- An ownership cycle does not conform (§47). -/
example : ¬ StaticsConf [((none, some 1, 0), true), ((none, some 0, 0), true)] :=
  fun h => h.owner_acyclic 0 (.tail (.single rfl) rfl)

end StaticsExamples

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.Derived
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Statics

/-!
# Renaming of identities: the initial state

Two `StaticsOK` numberings of one statics declaration related by a consistent renumbering
(`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` §47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2) have
corresponding initial states: the place renaming `Renumbered.π` and the root-authority renaming
`Renumbered.α` relate `S3.init` of both numberings (`Renumbered.initSim`).
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename

variable {statics : Statics} {σ : List Nat}

/-! ## Two numberings of one declaration (§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2) -/

/-- Two `StaticsOK` numberings of one declaration (§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2): `statics`
and its consistent renumbering by the permutation `σ`. -/
structure Renumbered (statics : Statics) (σ : List Nat) : Prop where
  perm : σ.Perm (List.range statics.length)
  cons : ConsistentRenumbering σ statics
  ok : StaticsOK statics
  ok' : StaticsOK (renumber σ statics)

/-- The place renaming of a renumbering (§49, last paragraph): old static `x` is new place
`σ.idxOf x`; identity from `statics.length` on. -/
def Renumbered.π (h : Renumbered statics σ) : Ren := Ren.ofPerm σ statics.length h.perm

/-- Old position of the root authority at each new position (§47; `S3.init` lists root
authorities in `rootIdx` order): new position `j'` holds the root of new root static `R'[j']`,
old static `π.g R'[j']`, whose old position is its index in the old `rootIdx`. -/
def rootPerm (statics : Statics) (σ : List Nat) (π : Ren) : List Nat :=
  (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1))).map fun i' =>
    (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).idxOf (π.g i')

/-! ## Proof support: the initial places (§47) -/

/-- Place of a static entry in `S3.init` (§47): its parent, its owning static or frame 0, its
kind. -/
private def initPlace (e : (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool) : Place :=
  ⟨e.1.1, match e.1.2.1 with | some o => .place o | none => .frame 0, e.1.2.2⟩

/-- The places of `S3.init` are the declared statics (§47). -/
private theorem init_P_get (st : Statics) (q : Nat) :
    (S3.init st).P[q]? = (st[q]?).map initPlace := by
  have := shapeP_get_new [] (.frame 0) (st.map (·.1)) q
  rw [List.length_nil, Nat.zero_add] at this
  show (shapeP [] (.frame 0) (st.map (·.1)))[q]? = _
  rw [this, List.length_map]
  split
  · rename_i hq
    simp only [List.getElem?_map, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hq, Option.map_some, Option.bind_some,
      shapeOwner, initPlace, Option.getD_some]
    rfl
  · rename_i hq
    rw [List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 (by omega)]
    rfl

/-- `S3.init` has one place per static (§47). -/
private theorem init_P_length (st : Statics) : (S3.init st).P.length = st.length := by
  simp [S3.init, shapeP]

/-- Parents of the initial places are the declared parents (§47). -/
private theorem init_parentOf (st : Statics) (q : Nat) :
    parentOf (S3.init st).P q = staticParent st q := by
  unfold parentOf staticParent
  rw [init_P_get]
  cases st[q]? <;> rfl

/-- A static with a parent is declared (§47). -/
private theorem init_lt_of_staticParent {st : Statics} {x p : Nat}
    (h : staticParent st x = some p) : x < st.length := by
  unfold staticParent at h
  cases hx : st[x]? with
  | none => rw [hx] at h; cases h
  | some _ => exact (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 hx).1

/-- Root statics are the declared statics with no parent (§40, §47). -/
private theorem init_mem_rootIdx (st : Statics) (i : Nat) :
    i ∈ rootIdx (st.map (·.1)) ↔ ∃ e, st[i]? = some e ∧ e.1.1 = none := by
  simp only [rootIdx, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, List.length_map, List.getElem?_map]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hi, hn⟩
    refine ⟨st[i], List.getElem?_eq_getElem hi, ?_⟩
    simpa [List.getElem?_eq_getElem hi] using hn
  · rintro ⟨e, he, hn⟩
    exact ⟨(List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 he).1, by simp [he, hn]⟩

/-- `rootIdx` has no duplicate (§47). -/
private theorem init_rootIdx_nodup (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
    (rootIdx ls).Nodup :=
  List.nodup_range.filter _

/-- A renamed static entry is the renamed place (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
private theorem initPlace_mapRefs (π : Ren) (e : (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool) :
    initPlace (mapRefs π.f e) = (initPlace e).ren π := by
  obtain ⟨⟨p, o, k⟩, b⟩ := e
  cases o <;> rfl

/-! ## The place renaming (§47; §49, last paragraph) -/

/-- A renumbering keeps the number of statics (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Renumbered.length (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
    (renumber σ statics).length = statics.length := by
  simp [renumber, h.perm.length_eq]

/-- `π` below the number of statics is the position in `σ` (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Renumbered.π_lt (h : Renumbered statics σ) {x : Nat} (hx : x < statics.length) :
    h.π.f x = σ.idxOf x := by
  simp [Renumbered.π, Ren.ofPerm, hx]

/-- `π` is the identity from the number of statics on (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Renumbered.π_fix (h : Renumbered statics σ) {x : Nat} (hx : statics.length ≤ x) :
    h.π.f x = x := by
  simp [Renumbered.π, Ren.ofPerm, Nat.not_lt.2 hx]

/-- `ConsistentRenumbering.entry` with `σ.idxOf` replaced by `π.f` (§47; §49, last paragraph):
the references of a `StaticsOK` declaration are declared statics; both sides are `none` from the
number of statics on. -/
theorem Renumbered.entry (h : Renumbered statics σ) (x : Nat) :
    (renumber σ statics)[h.π.f x]? = (statics[x]?).map (mapRefs h.π.f) := by
  by_cases hx : x < statics.length
  · rw [h.π_lt hx, h.cons.entry x hx]
    cases he : statics[x]? with
    | none => rfl
    | some e =>
      have hc := StaticsConf.of_staticsOK h.ok
      have href : ∀ o : Option Nat, (∀ p, o = some p → p < statics.length) →
          o.map σ.idxOf = o.map h.π.f := by
        intro o ho
        cases o with
        | none => rfl
        | some p => simp [h.π_lt (ho p rfl)]
      have hp := href e.1.1 fun p hp => hc.parent_lt x p (by simp [staticParent, he, hp])
      have ho := href e.1.2.1 fun o ho => hc.owner_lt x o (by simp [staticOwner, he, ho])
      simp only [Option.map_some, mapRefs, hp, ho]
  · have hx' : statics.length ≤ x := Nat.not_lt.1 hx
    rw [h.π_fix hx', List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 (by rw [h.length]; exact hx'),
      List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 hx']
    rfl

/-- The places of both initial states correspond (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Renumbered.initP (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
    PRel h.π (S3.init statics).P (S3.init (renumber σ statics)).P where
  len := by rw [init_P_length, init_P_length, h.length]
  get q := by
    rw [init_P_get, init_P_get, h.entry]
    cases statics[q]? with
    | none => rfl
    | some e => exact congrArg some (initPlace_mapRefs h.π e)
  fix q hq := h.π_fix (by rwa [init_P_length] at hq)

/-- The owners of both initial states correspond (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
private theorem Renumbered.init_shapeOwner (h : Renumbered statics σ) (i : Nat) :
    shapeOwner ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)) (.frame 0) (h.π.f i) =
      (shapeOwner (statics.map (·.1)) (.frame 0) i).ren h.π := by
  unfold shapeOwner
  rw [List.getElem?_map, List.getElem?_map, h.entry]
  cases statics[i]? with
  | none => rfl
  | some e =>
    obtain ⟨⟨p, o, k⟩, b⟩ := e
    cases o <;> rfl

/-! ## The root-authority renaming (§47; §49, last paragraph) -/

/-- Root statics correspond, forward (§40, §47). -/
private theorem Renumbered.root_mem_f (h : Renumbered statics σ) (i : Nat) :
    h.π.f i ∈ rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)) ↔ i ∈ rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)) := by
  rw [init_mem_rootIdx, init_mem_rootIdx, h.entry]
  cases statics[i]? with
  | none => simp
  | some e => simp [mapRefs]

/-- Root statics correspond (§40, §47; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Renumbered.root_mem (h : Renumbered statics σ) (i' : Nat) :
    i' ∈ rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)) ↔ h.π.g i' ∈ rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)) :=
  h.π.mem_iff_g h.root_mem_f i'

/-- The root statics of both numberings correspond up to order (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Renumbered.rootIdx_perm (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
    (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1))).Perm
      ((rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).map h.π.f) :=
  h.π.perm_of_mem (init_rootIdx_nodup _) (init_rootIdx_nodup _) h.root_mem_f

/-- `rootPerm` is a permutation of the root-authority positions (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Renumbered.rootPerm_perm (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
    (rootPerm statics σ h.π).Perm (List.range (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).length) := by
  have hm : ∀ i' ∈ rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)),
      h.π.g i' ∈ rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)) := fun i' hi' => (h.root_mem i').1 hi'
  apply perm_range_of_nodup
  · unfold rootPerm List.Nodup
    rw [List.pairwise_map]
    refine (init_rootIdx_nodup _).imp_of_mem fun {a b} ha hb hab e => hab ?_
    have ga := List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hm a ha))
    have gb := List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hm b hb))
    have : h.π.g a = h.π.g b := by
      rw [← ga, ← gb]
      exact getElem_congr rfl e _
    rw [← h.π.fg a, this, h.π.fg]
  · intro a ha
    obtain ⟨i', hi', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 ha
    exact List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hm i' hi')
  · rw [rootPerm, List.length_map, h.rootIdx_perm.length_eq, List.length_map]

/-- The root-authority renaming of a renumbering (§47; §49, last paragraph): old root authority
`j` goes to the new position of the root of static `π.f R[j]`; identity from the number of root
authorities on. -/
def Renumbered.α (h : Renumbered statics σ) : Ren :=
  Ren.ofPerm (rootPerm statics σ h.π) _ h.rootPerm_perm

/-- `rootIdx_α`, read backward (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
private theorem Renumbered.rootIdx_αg (h : Renumbered statics σ) (j' : Nat) :
    (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)))[j']? =
      ((rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)))[h.α.g j']?).map h.π.f := by
  have hlen := h.rootIdx_perm.length_eq
  rw [List.length_map] at hlen
  simp only [Renumbered.α, Ren.ofPerm]
  split
  · rename_i hj
    have hj' : j' < (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1))).length := by
      simpa [rootPerm] using hj
    have hm := (h.root_mem _).1 (List.getElem_mem hj')
    simp only [rootPerm, List.getElem_map]
    rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem hm),
      List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem hm), Option.map_some, h.π.fg,
      List.getElem?_eq_getElem hj']
  · rename_i hj
    have hj' : (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1))).length ≤ j' := by
      simpa [rootPerm] using hj
    rw [List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 hj', List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 (hlen ▸ hj')]
    rfl

/-- Root authority `j` of `statics` and root authority `α.f j` of the renumbering hold the roots
of corresponding statics (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Renumbered.rootIdx_α (h : Renumbered statics σ) (j : Nat) :
    (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)))[h.α.f j]? =
      ((rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)))[j]?).map h.π.f := by
  have := h.rootIdx_αg (h.α.f j)
  rwa [h.α.gf] at this

/-! ## The initial states correspond (§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2) -/

/-- Parent and origin links of the initial state go to smaller identities (§47, §49.2, §49.5;
§49, last paragraph): `init_kinv`. -/
theorem init_down (hst : StaticsOK statics) : Down (S3.init statics) :=
  Down.of_wf3 (init_kinv hst).1.1

/-- The initial states of both numberings are related (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Renumbered.initRel (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
    SRel h.π h.α (S3.init statics) (S3.init (renumber σ statics)) where
  F := rfl
  nF := rfl
  P := h.initP
  I l := by
    show (if (((renumber σ statics)[h.π.f l]?).map (·.2)).getD false then InitSt.init
      else .uninit) = if ((statics[l]?).map (·.2)).getD false then .init else .uninit
    rw [h.entry, Option.map_map]
    rfl
  Alen := by simp [S3.init, h.rootIdx_perm.length_eq]
  A x := by
    simp only [S3.init, List.getElem?_map]
    rw [h.rootIdx_α]
    cases (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)))[x]? with
    | none => exact .none
    | some i =>
      exact .some ⟨rfl, rfl,
        footprint_perm_ren h.initP (init_down h.ok).1 (init_down h.ok').1 i,
        h.init_shapeOwner i, rfl⟩
  Afix x hx := by
    have hx' : (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).length ≤ x := by simpa [S3.init] using hx
    simp [Renumbered.α, Ren.ofPerm, Nat.not_lt.2 hx']
  D _ := by simp [S3.init]
  dead _ := rfl
  pins o := by simp only [S3.init, List.getElem?_nil]; exact .none

/-- `π` keeps the field order of the initial places (§63.2; §49, last paragraph):
`ConsistentRenumbering.field_order`. -/
theorem Renumbered.initSib (h : Renumbered statics σ) : SibMono h.π (S3.init statics).P := by
  intro x y p hx hy hxy
  rw [init_parentOf] at hx hy
  rw [h.π_lt (init_lt_of_staticParent hx), h.π_lt (init_lt_of_staticParent hy)]
  exact h.cons.field_order x y p hx hy hxy

/-- The simulation invariant holds between the initial states of both numberings (§47; §49, last
paragraph; §63.2). -/
theorem Renumbered.initSim (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
    Sim h.π h.α (S3.init statics) (S3.init (renumber σ statics)) :=
  ⟨h.initRel, init_down h.ok, init_down h.ok', h.initSib⟩

/-- Every `StaticsOK` declaration (§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2) is `Renumbered` with the
consistent renumbering that `StaticsConf.exists_renumber` builds from it
(`StaticsConf.of_staticsOK`). `Renumbered` asks `StaticsOK` of both numberings, so a conforming
declaration that is not `StaticsOK` is not related to its numbering by this theorem. -/
theorem StaticsConf.renumbered (hok : StaticsOK statics) : ∃ σ, Renumbered statics σ := by
  obtain ⟨σ, hp, hc, hok'⟩ := (StaticsConf.of_staticsOK hok).exists_renumber
  exact ⟨σ, hp, hc, hok, hok'⟩

/-! ## Non-vacuity (§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2) -/

namespace InitExamples

/-- Root static 0 with fields 1 and 2, and root static 3 (§47, §63.2). -/
def n1 : Statics := [((none, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 1), true),
  ((some 0, none, 2), true), ((none, none, 3), false)]

/-- `n1` and its renumbering by `[3, 0, 1, 2]` are two `StaticsOK` numberings of one declaration
(§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2). -/
theorem n1_renumbered : Renumbered n1 [3, 0, 1, 2] where
  perm := by decide
  cons := {
    entry := fun x hx => by
      have key : ∀ x ∈ List.range 4, (renumber [3, 0, 1, 2] n1)[[3, 0, 1, 2].idxOf x]? =
          (n1[x]?).map (mapRefs [3, 0, 1, 2].idxOf) := by
        decide
      exact key x (List.mem_range.2 hx)
    field_order := fun x y _ hx hy hxy => by
      have key : ∀ x ∈ List.range 4, ∀ y ∈ List.range 4, staticParent n1 x = staticParent n1 y →
          (staticParent n1 x).isSome → x < y → [3, 0, 1, 2].idxOf x < [3, 0, 1, 2].idxOf y := by
        decide
      exact key x (List.mem_range.2 (init_lt_of_staticParent hx)) y
        (List.mem_range.2 (init_lt_of_staticParent hy)) (hx.trans hy.symm) (by rw [hx]; rfl) hxy }
  ok := by decide
  ok' := by decide

/-- Both renamings are non-trivial (§49, last paragraph): `π` sends static 0 to 1 and 3 to 0,
`α` swaps the two root authorities. -/
example : n1_renumbered.π.f 0 = 1 ∧ n1_renumbered.π.f 3 = 0 ∧ n1_renumbered.α.f 0 = 1 ∧
    n1_renumbered.α.f 1 = 0 := by decide

/-- The initial states of both numberings of `n1` correspond (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main

/-!
# Renaming of identities: core definitions

Foundation of the renaming bisimulation of the access kernel for
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` §49, last paragraph: renamings of place and
authority identities (`Ren`), the relation they induce on places, authorities, pinning
obligations (§74, §75) and states (§38), the order facts carried along runs (`Down`, `SibMono`),
the renamed contract (§48, §80), the renamed operations (§60–§75), and the relation of outcomes
(§58). Generic lemmas on these relations, closed by symmetry.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

namespace Rename

/-! ## Renamings (§49, last paragraph) -/

/-- A renaming of identities (§49, last paragraph): a bijection of `Nat` with its inverse. -/
structure Ren where
  f : Nat → Nat
  g : Nat → Nat
  gf : ∀ i, g (f i) = i
  fg : ∀ i, f (g i) = i

/-- The identity renaming (§49, last paragraph). -/
def Ren.id : Ren := ⟨fun i => i, fun i => i, fun _ => rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- The inverse renaming (§49, last paragraph). -/
def Ren.symm (π : Ren) : Ren := ⟨π.g, π.f, π.fg, π.gf⟩

/-- Composition of renamings, `π` first (§49, last paragraph). -/
def Ren.comp (π' π : Ren) : Ren :=
  ⟨fun i => π'.f (π.f i), fun i => π.g (π'.g i), fun i => by simp [π'.gf, π.gf],
   fun i => by simp [π'.fg, π.fg]⟩

/-- Renaming of a permutation `τ` of `List.range n` (§49, last paragraph): old `x < n` goes to its
position in `τ`, new `i < n` comes from `τ[i]`; identity from `n` on. -/
def Ren.ofPerm (τ : List Nat) (n : Nat) (h : τ.Perm (List.range n)) : Ren where
  f x := if x < n then τ.idxOf x else x
  g i := if hi : i < τ.length then τ[i] else i
  gf x := by
    have hl : τ.length = n := by simpa using h.length_eq
    by_cases hx : x < n
    · have hm : x ∈ τ := h.mem_iff.2 (List.mem_range.2 hx)
      have hi := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem hm
      simp [hx, hi, List.getElem_idxOf hi]
    · simp [hx, hl]
  fg i := by
    have hl : τ.length = n := by simpa using h.length_eq
    have hnd : τ.Nodup := h.nodup_iff.2 List.nodup_range
    by_cases hi : i < τ.length
    · have hlt : τ[i] < n := List.mem_range.1 (h.mem_iff.1 (List.getElem_mem hi))
      simp only [hi, dite_true, hlt, ite_true]
      exact (List.Nodup.getElem_inj hnd).1
        (List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (List.getElem_mem hi)))
    · simp [hi, hl ▸ hi]

/-- The inverse of `π` maps forward by `π.g` (§49, last paragraph). -/
@[simp] theorem Ren.symm_f (π : Ren) (i : Nat) : π.symm.f i = π.g i := rfl

/-- The inverse of `π` maps backward by `π.f` (§49, last paragraph). -/
@[simp] theorem Ren.symm_g (π : Ren) (i : Nat) : π.symm.g i = π.f i := rfl

/-- The inverse of the inverse is the renaming (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.symm_symm (π : Ren) : π.symm.symm = π := rfl

/-- A renaming is injective (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.f_inj (π : Ren) {i j : Nat} : π.f i = π.f j ↔ i = j :=
  ⟨fun h => by rw [← π.gf i, h, π.gf], fun h => h ▸ rfl⟩

/-- A renaming is determined by its forward map (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.ext {π π' : Ren} (h : ∀ i, π.f i = π'.f i) : π = π' := by
  have hg : ∀ i, π.g i = π'.g i := fun i =>
    calc π.g i = π.g (π.f (π'.g i)) := by rw [h, π'.fg]
      _ = π'.g i := π.gf _
  obtain ⟨f, g, _, _⟩ := π
  obtain ⟨f', g', _, _⟩ := π'
  simp only [Ren.mk.injEq]
  exact ⟨funext h, funext hg⟩

/-- A renaming composed with its inverse is the identity (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.symm_comp (π : Ren) : π.symm.comp π = Ren.id := Ren.ext fun i => π.gf i

/-- Mapping by `π.f` then `π.g` is the identity on lists (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.map_gf (π : Ren) (l : List Nat) : (l.map π.f).map π.g = l := by
  simp [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, π.gf]

/-- Mapping by `π.g` then `π.f` is the identity on lists (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.map_fg (π : Ren) (l : List Nat) : (l.map π.g).map π.f = l := by
  simp [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, π.fg]

/-- Membership in a renamed list, read backward (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.mem_map (π : Ren) (l : List Nat) (y : Nat) : y ∈ l.map π.f ↔ π.g y ∈ l := by
  constructor
  · intro hy; obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hy; rwa [π.gf]
  · intro hy; exact List.mem_map.2 ⟨π.g y, hy, π.fg y⟩

/-- Membership of a renamed identity in a renamed list (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.mem_map_f (π : Ren) (l : List Nat) (x : Nat) : π.f x ∈ l.map π.f ↔ x ∈ l := by
  rw [π.mem_map, π.gf]

/-- The f-form of a membership correspondence gives its g-form (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.mem_iff_g (π : Ren) {L L' : List Nat} (h : ∀ x, π.f x ∈ L' ↔ x ∈ L) (y : Nat) :
    y ∈ L' ↔ π.g y ∈ L := by rw [← h, π.fg]

/-- Universal quantification over all identities, renamed (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.forall_iff (π : Ren) {Q Q' : Nat → Prop} (hQ : ∀ x, Q' (π.f x) ↔ Q x) :
    (∀ y, Q' y) ↔ ∀ x, Q x :=
  ⟨fun h x => (hQ x).1 (h _), fun h y => by rw [← π.fg y]; exact (hQ _).2 (h _)⟩

/-- Universal quantification over corresponding lists (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.forall_mem_iff (π : Ren) {L L' : List Nat} (hL : ∀ x, π.f x ∈ L' ↔ x ∈ L)
    {Q Q' : Nat → Prop} (hQ : ∀ x, Q' (π.f x) ↔ Q x) :
    (∀ y ∈ L', Q' y) ↔ ∀ x ∈ L, Q x :=
  ⟨fun h x hx => (hQ x).1 (h _ ((hL x).2 hx)),
   fun h y hy => by
    rw [← π.fg y] at hy ⊢; exact (hQ _).2 (h _ ((hL _).1 hy))⟩

/-- Existential quantification over corresponding lists (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.exists_mem_iff (π : Ren) {L L' : List Nat} (hL : ∀ x, π.f x ∈ L' ↔ x ∈ L)
    {Q Q' : Nat → Prop} (hQ : ∀ x, Q' (π.f x) ↔ Q x) :
    (∃ y ∈ L', Q' y) ↔ ∃ x ∈ L, Q x :=
  ⟨fun ⟨y, hy, hq⟩ => by
    rw [← π.fg y] at hy hq; exact ⟨_, (hL _).1 hy, (hQ _).1 hq⟩,
   fun ⟨x, hx, hq⟩ => ⟨_, (hL x).2 hx, (hQ x).2 hq⟩⟩

/-- Duplicate-free lists with corresponding members are permutations up to renaming (§42: sets
represented by lists; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.perm_of_mem (π : Ren) {L L' : List Nat} (hnd : L.Nodup) (hnd' : L'.Nodup)
    (h : ∀ x, π.f x ∈ L' ↔ x ∈ L) : L'.Perm (L.map π.f) := by
  have hm : (L.map π.f).Nodup :=
    List.pairwise_map.2 (hnd.imp fun hab e => hab ((Ren.f_inj π).1 e))
  refine (List.perm_ext_iff_of_nodup hnd' hm).2 fun y => ?_
  rw [π.mem_iff_g h, π.mem_map]

def DownA (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ j o, s.org j = some o → o < j

/-- Parent and origin links go to smaller identities (§49.2, §49.5; §49, last paragraph). -/
def Down (s : S3) : Prop := DownP s.P ∧ DownA s

/-- `π` keeps the order of the parts of every place, their positional field order (§63.2; §49,
last paragraph). -/
def SibMono (π : Ren) (P : List Place) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y p, parentOf P x = some p → parentOf P y = some p → x < y → π.f x < π.f y

/-- The simulation invariant (§49, last paragraph; §57): related states, both with downward
links, and `π` keeping field order (§63.2). -/
structure Sim (π α : Ren) (s s' : S3) : Prop where
  rel : SRel π α s s'
  down : Down s
  down' : Down s'
  sib : SibMono π s.P

/-- Owner-accepted hypothesis of 2026-11-06 on `Satisfiable` (§71, §48; §49, last paragraph): it
does not distinguish states equal up to permutation of footprint, anchor and pin-leaf lists
(§42, §44). -/
def KExt (k : K) : Prop :=
  ∀ p sh s t, SRel Ren.id Ren.id s t → k.Satisfiable p sh s → k.Satisfiable p sh t

end Rename

/-! ## Renamed contract and operations (§48, §60–§75, §80) -/

/-- The contract renamed (§48, §80; §49, last paragraph). `FreeCompat`'s `auth` is opaque
(§70.2); obligations keep their identities (§75); `Satisfiable` (§71) is read on related
states. -/
def K.rename (π α : Ren) (k : K) : K where
  DeclaredDisjoint r r' := k.DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.g) (r'.map π.g)
  SharedMutable l := k.SharedMutable (π.g l)
  Pinned l := k.Pinned (π.g l)
  ExternalDone o := k.ExternalDone o
  Deallocable p := k.Deallocable (π.g p)
  FreeCompat p a := k.FreeCompat (π.g p) a
  Satisfiable p sh t := ∃ t₀, SRel π α t₀ t ∧ k.Satisfiable (π.g p) sh t₀

/-- Arguments renamed (§60–§75; §49, last paragraph). Shapes are not renamed (§71.1, §72.2:
fresh parents); `auth` is opaque (§70.2); `o` is an obligation identity (§75). -/
def KernelOp.ren (π α : Ren) : KernelOp → KernelOp
  | .derive src region m => .derive (α.f src) (region.map π.f) m
  | .split src rs => .split (α.f src) (rs.map (·.map π.f))
  | .release a => .release (α.f a)
  | .transfer src dst => .transfer (π.f src) (π.f dst)
  | .depend q x => .depend (π.f q) (α.f x)
  | .enter ps ls => .enter (ps.map α.f) ls
  | .exit => .exit
  | .read a ls => .read (α.f a) (ls.map π.f)
  | .write a ls => .write (α.f a) (ls.map π.f)
  | .writeShared a ls => .writeShared (α.f a) (ls.map π.f)
  | .pin p => .pin (π.f p)
  | .unpin o => .unpin o
  | .endUse p => .endUse (π.f p)
  | .free p auth => .free (π.f p) auth
  | .alloc pr ow ls => .alloc (π.f pr) (π.f ow) ls
  | .store a p => .store (α.f a) (π.f p)

namespace Rename

/-- Contracts corresponding under the renaming, `Satisfiable` excepted (§48, §80; §49, last
paragraph). -/
structure KCorr (π α : Ren) (k k' : K) : Prop where
  dd : ∀ r r', k'.DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.f) (r'.map π.f) ↔ k.DeclaredDisjoint r r'
  shared : ∀ l, k'.SharedMutable (π.f l) ↔ k.SharedMutable l
  pinned : ∀ l, k'.Pinned (π.f l) ↔ k.Pinned l
  done : ∀ o, k'.ExternalDone o ↔ k.ExternalDone o
  dealloc : ∀ p, k'.Deallocable (π.f p) ↔ k.Deallocable p
  compat : ∀ p a, k'.FreeCompat (π.f p) a ↔ k.FreeCompat p a

/-- Outcomes related by the renaming (§58; §49, last paragraph). -/
def OutRel (π α : Ren) : Outcome3 S3 → Outcome3 S3 → Prop
  | .ok t, .ok t' => SRel π α t t'
  | .reject, .reject => True
  | .fail, .fail => True
  | _, _ => False

/-- Outcome relations corresponding in both directions (§58; §49, last paragraph). -/
def StepCorr (π α : Ren) (R R' : Outcome3 S3 → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ o, R o → ∃ o', R' o' ∧ OutRel π α o o') ∧ ∀ o', R' o' → ∃ o, R o ∧ OutRel π α o o'

/-! ## Generic lemmas on the relations (§49, last paragraph) -/

section
variable {π π' α α' : Ren} {s s' s'' : S3} {P P' P'' : List Place}

/-- Related place lists have related bounds (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PRel.lt_iff (hP : PRel π P P') (q : Nat) : π.f q < P'.length ↔ q < P.length := by
  have := hP.get q
  · have := hs _ _ _ (hpar y p hy) (hpar x p hx) hgt
    rw [π.fg, π.fg] at this; omega

/-- Field order depends only on the parent links (§63.2; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SibMono.congr {P₁ : List Place} (hpar : parentOf P₁ = parentOf P) (hs : SibMono π P) :
    SibMono π P₁ := by
  intro x y p hx hy; rw [hpar] at hx hy; exact hs x y p hx hy

/-- Symmetry of the simulation invariant (§49, last paragraph; §57). -/
theorem Sim.symm (hS : Sim π α s s') : Sim π.symm α.symm s' s where
  rel := hS.rel.symm
  down := hS.down'
  down' := hS.down
  sib := SibMono.symm hS.rel.P hS.sib

/-- The renamed contract corresponds to the contract (§48, §80; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem KCorr.rename (π α : Ren) (k : K) : KCorr π α k (k.rename π α) where
  dd r r' := by simp only [K.rename, Ren.map_gf]
  shared l := by simp only [K.rename, π.gf]
  pinned l := by simp only [K.rename, π.gf]
  done _ := Iff.rfl
  dealloc p := by simp only [K.rename, π.gf]
  compat p a := by simp only [K.rename, π.gf]

/-- Symmetry of corresponding contracts (§48, §80; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem KCorr.symm {k k' : K} (hK : KCorr π α k k') : KCorr π.symm α.symm k' k where
  dd r r' := by
    have := hK.dd (r.map π.g) (r'.map π.g)
    rw [Ren.map_fg, Ren.map_fg] at this; exact this.symm
  shared l := by have := hK.shared (π.g l); rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm
  pinned l := by have := hK.pinned (π.g l); rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm
  done o := (hK.done o).symm
  dealloc p := by have := hK.dealloc (π.g p); rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm
  compat p a := by have := hK.compat (π.g p) a; rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm

/-- `DDSound` (§80, §23) is invariant under renaming of the contract (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem ddSound_rename (π α : Ren) (k : K) : DDSound (k.rename π α) ↔ DDSound k := by
  constructor
  · intro h r r' hd l hl hl'
    have hd' : (k.rename π α).DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.f) (r'.map π.f) := by
      simp only [K.rename, Ren.map_gf]; exact hd
    exact h _ _ hd' (π.f l) ((π.mem_map_f _ _).2 hl) ((π.mem_map_f _ _).2 hl')
  · intro h r r' hd l hl hl'
    exact h _ _ hd (π.g l) (List.mem_map_of_mem hl) (List.mem_map_of_mem hl')

/-- Guarded steps with corresponding preconditions and related effects correspond (§58; §49, last
paragraph). -/
theorem guarded_corr {Pre Pre' : Prop} {e e' : S3} (hp : Pre' ↔ Pre)
    (he : Pre → SRel π α e e') : StepCorr π α (Guarded Pre e) (Guarded Pre' e') := by
  constructor
  · intro o ho
    cases ho with
    | ok hpre => exact ⟨.ok e', .ok (hp.2 hpre), he hpre⟩
    | reject hpre => exact ⟨.reject, .reject (fun h' => hpre (hp.1 h')), trivial⟩
  · intro o' ho'
    cases ho' with
    | ok hpre => exact ⟨.ok e, .ok (hp.1 hpre), he (hp.1 hpre)⟩
    | reject hpre => exact ⟨.reject, .reject (fun h => hpre (hp.2 h)), trivial⟩

end

/-- Renaming the arguments by the inverse, then by the renaming, gives the operation back (§60–§75;
§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem KernelOp.ren_symm_ren (π α : Ren) (op : KernelOp) :
    (op.ren π.symm α.symm).ren π α = op := by
  cases op <;>
    simp [KernelOp.ren, List.map_map, Function.comp_def, π.fg, α.fg]

/-- Renaming the arguments, then by the inverse, gives the operation back (§60–§75; §49, last
paragraph). -/
theorem KernelOp.symm_ren_ren (π α : Ren) (op : KernelOp) :
    (op.ren π α).ren π.symm α.symm = op :=
  KernelOp.ren_symm_ren π.symm α.symm op

end Rename

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.
